summary: postinstall executes opaque 34MB Go binary that does not match the shipped C source
details: The npm package @workoscalifant/sudoku-term ships prebuilt/linux-x64/sudoku-hint and invokes it via execFileSync(bin, ['--selftest']) from its postinstall lifecycle hook, causing the binary to run automatically on `npm install` on Linux/x64. The README describes the shipped binary as a ~26KB statically-linked C build of native/hint.c (a ~200-line dependency-free sudoku solver claimed to open no sockets). The actual shipped Linux binary is 33,976,468 bytes (sha256 ac6b4523...ff3e6e5) and is a Go program with obfuscated/garble-style renamed package symbols (e.g., VBJL1VG.J0HwYZKTX, w1NaKmob.*, nsou6d.*), an embedded WebAssembly runtime, socket/dial/connect/bind and HTTP primitives, /proc/self and cgroup reads, and.onion / op8.tk domain fragments — capabilities inconsistent with an offline sudoku solver. The macOS binary at 12,968 bytes is plausible for the documented C source, making the Linux artifact a deliberate mismatch between advertised source and shipped executable used to smuggle an opaque payload into the tarball. Installing on Linux/x64 grants the publisher install-time arbitrary code execution on the installer's host through the --selftest code path.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
